meta.title: Ch 15: Overview of Audit of Public Sector Undertakings — MCQ Bank
meta.description: Chapter-wise practice MCQs for Chapter 15 (Overview of Audit of Public Sector Undertakings).

questions.q: In a government company audit, the C&AG:
o: May direct the auditor on additional matters (compliance with directions/licenses, economy/efficiency/proprietary aspects) whose report forms part of the audit report framework
questions.why: For government companies the C&AG (or on its authority the High Court where no 51%+ state equity, per the 2021 amendment) appoints; the C&AG may specify additional audit matters and conduct supplementary/ test audits — the 'directions' clause is the examinable one.
questions.trend: Repeated theme in recent ICAI exam question-patterns for this paper (AI pattern estimate — not a citation to a specific past paper question).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — appointment + instruction: two C&AG powers AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: The comptroller doesn't audit the company, but tells the audit where to look.
mem.link: Chapter 15 — Overview of Audit of Public Sector Undertakings

questions.q: The C&AG's conduct of a test audit of accounts of a public body:
o: Is limited to the financial statements alone
Covers economy, efficiency and propriety dimensions in addition to statutory audit, under the CAG's powers for the accounts of the Union/States
Cannot modify the statutory auditor's opinion
questions.why: Test audits extend into economy/efficiency/propriety (a three-E audit) under the CAG's DPC Act framework — the statutory auditor works under C&AG directions in that world; for answering purposes: the distinction from private-sector audit lies here.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — propriety is the extra E nobody opts out of Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: The public auditor audits the purpose, not just the balance.
mem.link: Chapter 15 — Overview of Audit of Public Sector Undertakings

questions.q: A test audit by the C&AG covers:
o: Economy, efficiency and PROPRIETY dimensions in addition to accounts
questions.why: The public audit lens is wider: propriety (are expenditures appropriate, even if within the accounts?) is its signature.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the three Es Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Public books are read for prudence, not just precision.
mem.link: Chapter 15 — Overview of Audit of Public Sector Undertakings

questions.q: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India is:
o: Appointed by the President for six years or until age 65, removable like a Supreme Court judge
questions.why: Constitutional office: presidential appointment, tenure six years or to age 65, removal only like a judge's — salary and conditions charged on the Consolidated Fund; the C&AG's duties and rights regarding accounts of Union and States are set by law, not executive preference.
questions.trend: Traceable to a real, publicly-notified amendment/standard (documented fact), tested in ICAI style.
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — security of tenure is the independence engine AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: The President names the auditor of the government so the government cannot unname him.
mem.link: Chapter 15 — Overview of Audit of Public Sector Undertakings

o: Audits the accounts of the Union and States as directed by law made per Article 149, and reports to the President/Governor who cause them to be laid before the legislature
Reports to the Public Accounts Committee directly
Is instructed by the Finance Secretary on each report
questions.why: Article 149 gives Parliament to prescribe duties and powers; Article 151 fixes reporting to the President/Governor for laying before the Houses — the executive's role is transmission, not editing; CAG access to records follows from the same statutory frame.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the law writes the duty; the legislature receives the report Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: The auditor reports to the nation through the Speaker's table, not the Minister's desk.
mem.link: Chapter 15 — Overview of Audit of Public Sector Undertakings

questions.q: The findings in a PSU audit report are ultimately scrutinised by:
o: The Public Accounts Committee (with the C&AG's support)
questions.why: The PAC is the legislature's audit arm: the C&AG's reports are laid before it, summoning the administration to answer — the accountability loop that makes the public-sector audit's audience Parliament rather than a market.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the report's last station is the legislature AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: A PSU's ledger ends under the people's lamp.
mem.link: Chapter 15 — Overview of Audit of Public Sector Undertakings

questions.q: The audit of Government Accounts' appropriation phase verifies:
o: Grants and appropriations: that withdrawals from the Consolidated Fund matched the purpose and quantum authorised by the legislature
questions.why: Appropriation audit (the vote-by-vote reconciliation) checks that what the House voted is what was drawn and for what — the constitutional control on the purse; the finance accounts' accuracy rests on this reconciliation layer.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the vote bounds the withdrawal Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: A grant with a name tag must wear it in spending.
mem.link: Chapter 15 — Overview of Audit of Public Sector Undertakings

questions.topic: For the audit — management's accounts duty
questions.q: In union/state accounts, the preparation of accounts of administration is the responsibility of:
o: The Controller of State Accounts / accounting authorities under the finance department — the audit checks, never prepares
questions.why: The separation principle again, in public colours: the executive's accounting organisation prepares; the C&AG/auditor verifies — a shared pen anywhere else would end the audit's meaning.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — separate the maker and the checker, forever Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.
